title: Generating Human Gastruloids from Human Embryonic Stem Cells
protocol: Maintain hESCs in Nutristem medium on vitronectin N-precoated tissue culture-treated plastic.
Exchange the culture medium daily for fresh, room-temperature warmed Nutristem medium.
Culture hESCs for at least two passages post-thawing before refreezing.
Do not maintain hESCs beyond six passages post-thawing to avoid variable effects.
Maintain stocks under antibiotic-free conditions to quickly identify any microbial infections.
Allow Nutristem media to warm to room temperature before thawing hESCs.
Prepare vitronectin coated wells of a 6-well plate by adding 0.5 μg/cm² vitronectin in PBS-/- to each well.
Leave the prepared wells at room temperature for one hour or longer periods at 4°C wrapped with parafilm before plating.
Prepare Nutristem media for plating with 1:1000 ROCK inhibitor at a volume of 3 mL per 3 cm well.
Place 9 mL Nutristem media in a 15 mL falcon tube as resuspension medium.
Thaw cryovial(s) by suspending them in a 37°C water bath until almost all the vial is liquid (approx. 30 seconds).
Apply 1 mL of prepared resuspension medium drop-wise to the cryovial.
Transfer all liquid from the cryovial into the resuspension medium falcon tube.
Centrifuge cells in resuspension medium at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in plating medium.
Remove vitronectin coating from wells, then transfer cell suspension to new wells.
Place cells in a humidified incubator (37°C, 5% CO2).
The next day, replace media with fresh Nutristem without ROCK inhibitor.
Remove medium from cells, and wash cells with 3 mL PBS-/- per well of a 6-well plate.
Add 2 mL of room-temperature 0.5 mM EDTA in PBS-/- per well of a 6-well plate.
Place in the incubator for 4.5 minutes.
Tap against solid surface or gently pipette to dislodge cells as clusters.
Check under a dissection/benchtop microscope that this has occurred before continuing.
Transfer cell suspension to prepared falcon tube with PBS-/-.
Centrifuge cells at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant and resuspend in 1 mL KSR+DMSO.
Transfer cell suspension to cryovial and quickly transfer to a Coolcell/’Mr. Frosty’ and to -80°C storage.
The next day, transfer cryovial(s) to -140/150°C liquid nitrogen storage.
Wash cells once with 3 mL PBS-/- per well of a 6-well plate.
Add 2 mL of room-temperature 0.5 mM EDTA in PBS-/- per well of a 6-well plate.
Place the plate in the incubator for 4.5 minutes.
Carefully remove EDTA using a suction pump, being careful not to dislodge cells from the surface.
Add 2 mL PBS-/- before tapping against a solid surface to dislodge the cells as clusters.
Check under a dissection/benchtop microscope that cells have dislodged into clusters.
Collect cells using a P1000 and transfer to a 15 mL falcon tube containing 8 mL PBS-/-.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL fresh Nutristem carefully.
Plate cells in 3 mL of Nutristem per well of a vitronectin-coated 6-well plate, using a ratio between 1:4 to 1:20 based on original cell density and cluster size.
Dissociate and passage cells as described in the section describing hESC passaging.
Closely monitor cells daily to determine the correct timepoint to perform pre-treatment.
Prepare vitronectin-coated wells of a 6-well plate by putting 0.5 μg/cm² vitronectin in PBS-/- into the wells.
Leave the prepared wells at room temperature for 1 hour before plating, or store them at 4°C wrapped with parafilm for longer periods.
Wash cells once with 3 mL PBS-/- per well of a 6-well plate.
Add 2 mL of room-temperature 0.5 mM EDTA per well of a 6-well plate.
Place the plate in the incubator for 4.5 minutes before gently tapping against a solid surface to dislodge the cells.
Dissociate the colonies into a single cell suspension with a P1000 micropipette tip by pipetting up-and-down 5-10 times and ejecting the suspension forcefully against the bottom of the well.
Collect cells using a P1000 and then transfer to a 15 mL falcon tube with 8 mL PBS-/-.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant and fully resuspend cells in 200-1000 μL Nutristem depending on pellet size.
Check under dissection microscope that the cells are in a single-cell suspension.
Count cells using an automated cell counter or haematocytometer.
Add 60,000 to 80,000 cells to 3 mL of room-temperature replating medium for each well of a 6-well plate.
Remove vitronectin coating from the 6-well plate and add cell suspension to the well.
Place cells in the incubator. Cells should be left to grow for 4 days (with fresh Nutristem exchange daily) before pre-treatment.
Prepare Nutristem supplemented with between 3-3.5 μM Chiron, depending on cell line.
Aspirate Nutristem medium from cells and replace with Chiron-supplemented medium.
Pre-warm EDTA and E6 to room temperature.
Prepare aggregation medium by supplementing E6 with 0.5-3 μM Chiron and 1:2000 ROCK inhibitor for each 96-well plate of aggregates, typically using 5 mL per plate.
Consider titrating the concentration of ROCK inhibitor to 1:1000 if aggregation is poor when working with new cell lines.
Aspirate the medium from the 6-well plate.
Rinse gently with 3 mL PBS-/-.
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed 0.5 mM EDTA.
Place in the incubator for 4.5 minutes.
Gently tap against a solid surface to dislodge the cells.
Dissociate the colonies into a single cell suspension with a P1000 micropipette tip by pipetting up-and-down 5-10 times and ejecting the suspension forcefully against the bottom of the well.
Observe cell suspension under an inverted benchtop microscope to check for single-cell suspension.
Pass cell suspension through a filter if necessary.
Collect cells using a P1000.
Transfer collected cells to a 15 mL falcon tube with 8 mL PBS-/-.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Fully resuspend in 200-1000 μL of E6 depending on pellet size.
Load the counting slide of an automated cell counter with 75 μL of cell suspension.
Determine the density of the cell suspension.
Check the amount of debris in the suspension using the Moxi Population Index (MPI).
Aim for an MPI value greater than 0.7 to minimize debris and contaminants.
Determine the volume of cell suspension required to produce a concentration of 10-20 cells/μL of aggregation medium.
Add the calculated volume of cell suspension to the required amount of aggregation medium.
Mix well by inverting the mixture or pipetting it up and down within the reservoir.
Transfer the mixed solution to a sterile reservoir.
Pipette 40 μL of plating suspension into each well of a sterile, U-bottomed non-tissue culture-treated 96-well plate.
Confirm that cells can be seen within each well using the inverted benchtop microscope.
Centrifuge the plates using a plate centrifuge at 700 rpm for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Return the plate to the incubator for 24 hours to allow aggregation.
Pre-warm E6 medium to room temperature.
Transfer 150 μL of E6 medium to each well using the multichannel micropipette and a sterile plastic reservoir.
Return the plate to the incubator for a further 24 hours.
Pre-warm E6 medium to room temperature.
Carefully remove 150 μL of medium from each well using a multichannel micropipette.
Hold the pipette at an angle to aspirate slowly from the side of each well.
Add 150 μL of fresh E6 to each well using the multichannel micropipette.
Return the plate to the incubator.
Repeat steps 20-23 each day for the duration of the protocol.
